primary_secondary.note: Both describe the authors' own Delphi study and survey for instrument validation.

study_type.claude: Survey (quantitative instrument development and validation: Delphi, online survey, EFA, CFA)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (Delphi, online survey, EFA, CFA/SEM)
study_type.note: Same design described (literature-derived items, Delphi content validity, online questionnaire, EFA and CFA), but Claude labels it quantitative (Survey) and NotebookLM labels it Mixed methods.

research_method.claude: Quantitative instrument development and validation: literature-derived preliminary items; one-round email Delphi (4 experts, Lawshe CVR); online survey (260 distributed, 225 used); normality checks; EFA (PCA, direct oblimin), Cronbach's alpha; CFA in AMOS (convergent/discriminant validity, model fit, second-order nomological validity)
research_method.nlm: Delphi study for content validity (4 experts), online survey (225 valid of 260), EFA, CFA/SEM
research_method.value: Psychometric instrument development and validation: preliminary items from the literature; one-round Delphi with 4 experts for content validity (Lawshe CVR); online survey (260 distributed, 225 responses analysed); EFA (principal component extraction, direct oblimin rotation) with Cronbach's alpha; second-order CFA (convergent and discriminant validity, model fit, nomological validity)
research_method.note: Main-survey scale omitted: NotebookLM says 7-point Likert, Claude says the scale is stated only for the Delphi. One-round Delphi and EFA settings reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; 'S and L companies' in South Korea, IT software solutions and service integration (AI/NLP, smart factory, blockchain, cloud data analysis); respondents in DL technology planning, design and development; 225 analysed; 4 Delphi experts from academia/industry
context.nlm: Industry; S and L IT companies in South Korea (software solutions, service integration, AI/NLP, smart factory, blockchain, cloud data analysis); 225 valid responses of 260; 4 Delphi experts
context.value: industry; IT companies ('S and L companies') in South Korea providing software solutions and service integration (AI/NLP models, smart factory, blockchain, cloud data analysis); 225 employees in deep-learning technology planning, design and development analysed (260 surveyed), plus a 4-expert Delphi panel

ai_discussed.note: Object is the developer experience of developers using a deep-learning platform (for building ML models). Claude does not treat AI as a topic (AI not a research method, no AI productivity impact); NotebookLM marks Yes because the DX concerns DL platforms. Author to judge whether this is AI as a developer tool or only as application domain.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not reported by either.

data_window.claude: Delphi 4-23 January 2021; online survey 8 February-26 March 2021
data_window.note: Only Claude states the data collection period; NotebookLM gives no dates.

cat_productivity.note: Claude: perceived productivity/efficiency items were discarded (Delphi CVR, EFA loadings). NotebookLM tags the Likert item 'platform is fast' (C8) as DevEx/Productivity, but it is a perceptual rating of the platform, not an output metric.

cat_quality.note: Items on stability and 'high-quality value' are perceptions of the platform, not software quality metrics.

cat_collaboration.note: Collaboration factors appear only in cited literature (Parviainen et al.).

cat_satisfaction.note: Affective component (intrigue, attractiveness, positive feeling, felt value), tagged Satisfaction by both; DX as a broad affective/attitudinal construct.

cat_activity.note: NotebookLM tags the behavioral items (usage intention, willingness to pay) as DevEx/Activity, but these are intentions, not repository activity.

cat_devex.note: Both label the constructs DevEx, but the framework is Fagerholm & Munch (2012) cognition/affection/conation, not the Noda/Storey/Forsgren DevEx framework.

cat_survey.note: Online questionnaire (225 respondents) and 7-point Likert Delphi; all metrics are perceptual items.

evidence.quote: A Delphi study as well as a series of statistical methodologies including the assessment of data normality, common method bias, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis were utilized to determine the reliability and validity
The Delphi evaluation tool was constructed based on closed-ended questions using a 7-point Likert scale

For the main survey in this study, a questionnaire was distributed to 260 employees in the industry, including S and L companies in South Korea. Their job description involves DL technology planning, design, and development.
The survey was conducted based on an online survey tool from 8 February to 26 March 2021. Insincere responses were excluded, and survey data from 225 employees were used in the final analysis.
Direct oblimin and principal component analysis were used for factor analysis rotation and factor extraction, respectively, to perform the exploratory factor analysis.
Affection includes the developer's feelings or emotions, such as positive emotion or pleasure.
E3. Developers get a positive feeling from the platform.
